purpose: Test unseen-case generalization against public, externally-authored incidents without changing the frozen core.

can_support: counterexample discovery against the frozen evaluator

authoring_boundary: The incident-to-kernel translation is authored in Aegis and is therefore not independent implementation evidence. Source incidents and fixes are external ground truth; the frozen evaluator and oracle are unchanged.

issue.title: migrate adopt-ent: frozen Ent baseline misses raw-SQL-only objects (distributed_locks) — api crashloops after adoption

ground_truth.root_cause: The adoption baseline was Ent-derived and omitted raw-SQL-only distributed_locks objects; stamping the database at the frozen baseline prevented the earlier raw SQL migration from replaying.
ground_truth.consequence: Migration reported success through head but the API crashlooped because the required sequence/table was absent.

fix.summary: Add an idempotent forward migration restoring missing distributed-lock objects and cover missing/existing state.

kernel_mapping.rationale: A known material state distinction existed outside the baseline/profile view. Automatic continuation under a basis that cannot distinguish required raw-SQL state is incomplete.

issue.title: Concurrent invoice collection shares the same error variable across goroutines

ground_truth.root_cause: Concurrent customer collection goroutines reused the same outer error variable, allowing one customer's result to overwrite another customer's result.
ground_truth.consequence: Outcome/error attribution could be assigned to the wrong concurrent customer collection.

fix.summary: Use goroutine-local collection errors and add a deterministic concurrent regression test.

kernel_mapping.rationale: A closure/result claim must remain bound to the exact effect lineage; cross-customer result contamination cannot support a verified exact outcome.

ground_truth.root_cause: A message could be written to PostgreSQL, lose its RabbitMQ ACK, then be redelivered; the affected older deployment lacked the conflict handling needed to make the replay safe.
ground_truth.consequence: The same logical message entered repeated duplicate-key failure/redelivery loops after a possible prior effect.

fix.summary: Maintainer confirmed ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING was already added in v0.85.5; upgrading from chart engine v0.84.0 brought in the fix.

kernel_mapping.rationale: After a possible prior effect, redelivery is not safe merely because it is a retry; an idempotency/conflict rule must make the same-effect replay safe.

issue.title: [BUG] Go SDK: child Run can hang after child already COMPLETED (shared result listener)

ground_truth.root_cause: A shared workflow-result listener could race with clean exit/reconnect so a completed child result was not delivered to the waiter.
ground_truth.consequence: The parent could time out and retry, spawning a second child and therefore duplicate side effects despite the first child already being complete.

fix.summary: Make the clean-stop decision and listener gate release atomic so registered work keeps the result listener alive.

kernel_mapping.rationale: Missing completion observation cannot justify minting a second effect when the first may already have completed.

issue.title: [BUG] Running Python durable tasks ignore cancellation

ground_truth.root_cause: Cancellation omitted the durable invocation count, so the worker looked up a different task key and failed to target the running durable invocation.
ground_truth.consequence: A cancellation action was not bound to the exact current execution identity and the task continued.

fix.summary: Send the durable invocation count on cancel, matching the identity used on start.

kernel_mapping.rationale: A consequential cancel must bind the exact material execution identity; omitting invocation identity makes the action revision/target ambiguous.

issue.title: dropOnUpdateTrigger unconditional in down() causes rollback failure

ground_truth.root_cause: Migration up() conditionally created the WebAuthn table/trigger, while down() unconditionally tried to drop the trigger even when this migration had not created the relation.
ground_truth.consequence: Rollback assumed a state transition that had not occurred and failed on a database whose relevant pre-state differed.

fix.summary: Mirror the state guard in down() with a hasTable check before dropping the trigger.

kernel_mapping.rationale: Whether this migration created/owns the rollback target is consequence-relevant state and must be bound before the rollback effect.

stop_rule: If any incident requires changing the frozen oracle, evaluator ordering, or semantic meaning to obtain the expected safety disposition, record D03-A as a falsification failure. Do not edit candidate-kernel-contract-v1 in place.
